Traditional Swiss Cheese Fondue

Served at: Berchtoldstag

Serves 4-6Prep 15 minCook 15 min

Swiss Cheese Fondue is a beloved communal dish, perfect for the festive atmosphere of Berchtoldstag on January 2nd. This holiday, celebrated in several Swiss cantons, is a time for family and friends to gather, and a warm, bubbling pot of fondue provides a cozy and interactive centerpiece for winter celebrations, symbolizing togetherness and good cheer.

Ingredients

  • 1 clove garlic, peeled
  • 1 pound (450 g) Gruyère cheese, grated
  • 1/2 pound (225 g) Emmentaler cheese, grated
  • 2 cups (470 ml) dry white wine (such as Fendant or Sauvignon Blanc)
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) cornstarch
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) Kirsch (cherry brandy)
  • 1/4 teaspoon freshly grated nutmeg
  • Pinch of black pepper
  • 1-2 loaves crusty day-old bread (such as baguette or rustic white bread), cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes

Method

  1. Rub the inside of a heavy-bottomed pot (a 'caquelon' if you have one) thoroughly with the peeled garlic clove, then discard the garlic.
  2. In a small bowl, whisk together the cornstarch and Kirsch until smooth; set aside.
  3. Pour the dry white wine into the garlic-rubbed pot and heat over medium-low heat until it just begins to simmer, but do not boil.
  4. Gradually add the grated Gruyère and Emmentaler cheeses to the wine, a handful at a time, stirring continuously in a figure-eight motion with a wooden spoon until each addition is melted and smooth before adding more.
  5. Once all the cheese is melted and the fondue is creamy, stir in the cornstarch-Kirsch mixture.
  6. Continue to stir gently for 1-2 minutes until the fondue thickens slightly and is smooth and glossy.
  7. Season the fondue with freshly grated nutmeg and a pinch of black pepper.
  8. Carefully transfer the fondue to a preheated fondue pot set over a low flame or burner to keep it warm and bubbling gently.
  9. Serve immediately with the cubed bread for dipping.

Tips

  • To prevent the fondue from separating or becoming stringy, add the cheese gradually and stir constantly in a figure-eight motion.
  • If the fondue becomes too thick, stir in a tablespoon or two of warm white wine. If it's too thin, mix a little more cornstarch with Kirsch and stir it in.
  • Traditionally, if someone drops their bread into the fondue, they might owe a round of drinks or a kiss to the person next to them!
